comparison: Both strongly support the SPARK-SPARKEL interaction findings (C6, C24-C27, C32-C33, C38, C41-C44). OpenEval emphasizes multiple independent experimental approaches and structural characterization. Peer reviewers praised the 'compelling evidence' and 'state-of-the-art proteomic methodologies.' Peer review also includes additional claims (C31, C34-C36, C39-C40, C45) related to sequence features and phylogenetics that OpenEval addresses separately.

Both support phylogenetic distribution claims (C34-C36). OpenEval notes the inference about ancestral presence is reasonable but alternative scenarios not ruled out. Peer reviewers accepted the phylogenetic analysis without concerns. Peer review R14 also includes C175-C176 about SPARKEL absence in Plasmodium, which OpenEval addresses in R21.

Both support reciprocal co-depletion findings (C46-C52). OpenEval acknowledges technical limitations of low protein abundance. Peer reviewers unanimously accepted phenotypic findings. Peer review R2 also includes time-course claims (C53-C60) that OpenEval addresses separately in R4.

Both support time-course phenotypic characterization (C53-C60). OpenEval emphasizes distinction between 3-hour and 24-hour timepoints with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers noted 'observations are masterfully backed up with validation' and accepted that phenotypes develop over time without questioning the molecular mechanism.

Both strongly support quantitative proteomics findings (C61-C68). OpenEval highlights TMT multiplexing and temporal dynamics. Peer reviewers praised 'sophisticated analysis techniques' and noted the work 'set a new benchmark.' Peer review R3 also includes C130 about temporal dynamics, which OpenEval addresses in R15.

Perfect alignment on phosphoproteomics analysis (C69-C79). Both strongly support the comprehensive dataset and statistical methods. OpenEval notes some effects may be indirect. Peer reviewers praised sophisticated analysis without raising concerns about data quality or interpretation, though Reviewer 3 mentioned 'incomplete data analysis' was improved in revision.

Both support TurboID proximity labeling results (C80-C83). OpenEval notes PKA C1 narrowly missing cutoffs suggests borderline significance. Peer reviewers accepted the data as supporting SPARK's role in regulating AGC kinases. Peer review R5 also includes C131 about spatial association, which OpenEval addresses in R15.

Perfect alignment on PKA C1/R regulation findings (C85-C91). Both support the integration of phosphoproteomics, qRT-PCR, immunofluorescence, and flow cytometry demonstrating post-translational regulation. Peer reviewers endorsed the multi-level validation approach, viewing it as 'masterfully backed up.'

Perfect alignment on PKG regulation findings (C92-C95). Both support the combination of phosphoproteomics with chemical-genetic validation. OpenEval notes the mechanism (reduced protein vs. activity) requires further investigation. Peer reviewers accepted the functional validation using PKG inhibitor sensitization without question.

Strong alignment on stage conversion/differentiation findings (C96-C106). Both support the multiple approaches including immunofluorescence, genetic epistasis with BFD1, and transcriptomics. OpenEval notes the molecular mechanism linking SPARK/PKA C3 to BFD1 remains unclear. Peer reviewers strongly endorsed findings, with Reviewer 2 noting the work 'backs up and extends' prior PKA C3 findings. Peer review excludes C98 that OpenEval includes.

Both support SPARK-PKA C3 interaction findings (C107-C110). OpenEval notes stoichiometry and functional significance require further investigation. Peer reviewers accepted the reciprocal IP approach and consistency with prior literature. Peer review R9 also includes C157 about PKA C3 association, which OpenEval addresses in R26.

Perfect alignment on differential PKA C3 regulation (C111-C113). Both support the distinction from PKA C1 regulation. OpenEval notes the trend toward increased PKA C3 is not statistically significant. Peer reviewers accepted this differential regulation as part of comprehensive characterization without challenge.

Perfect alignment on PKA C3 depletion phosphoproteomics (C114-C120). Both support the statistical analysis and comparative approaches. OpenEval notes the divergence in dense granule protein regulation is mechanistically unclear. Peer reviewers praised the sophisticated analysis techniques without questioning the interpretation.

Perfect alignment on the central model (C132, C145, C151, C179-C180). Both strongly support the proposed signaling pathway integrating genetic, proteomic, and phenotypic data. OpenEval notes direct biochemical evidence for SPARK kinase activity is lacking. Peer reviewers strongly endorsed the model, with Reviewer 2 stating the paper 'is not overreaching in its conclusions.'

Both support temporal dynamics findings (C130). OpenEval addresses this as a summary of time-course proteomics. Peer reviewers accepted the temporal characterization as part of the comprehensive proteomic analysis. OpenEval R15 also includes C131 about spatial association from TurboID, which peer review addresses in R5.

Perfect alignment on sequence features and phosphorylation sites (C134-C137, C158-C159). Both support the presence of FXXF motifs and T-loop phosphorylation changes. OpenEval notes functional importance of motifs not directly tested through mutagenesis. Peer reviewers accepted the structural features as supporting the proposed PDK1-like regulatory mechanism.

Both address PKG regulation mechanisms (C140-C141). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to conflicting evidence about T-loop phosphorylation essentiality and speculative conclusions without functional validation. Peer reviewers accepted the detailed phosphorylation site analyses as part of comprehensive characterization without questioning the interpretation. OpenEval R17 also includes C138-C139 not addressed in peer review.

OpenEval rates C142-C144 as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging mechanistic uncertainty about kinase down-regulation (dilution vs. ubiquitin-mediated degradation). The authors appropriately identify this as requiring further study. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically address these mechanistic uncertainties.

OpenEval supports activity-based regulation of PKA C3 (C160-C162), noting C162 is speculative about overlapping phosphosites reflecting direct differentiation targets. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers accepted PKA C3 findings broadly but did not separately evaluate these specific mechanistic claims.

Both address SPARK regulation mechanisms (C168, C174). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the proposal that SPARKEL complex modulates SPARK activity is speculative and co-depletion complicates interpretation. Peer reviewers also express UNCERTAINTY, with Reviewer 3 noting 'incomplete data analysis still needs to be addressed' and acknowledging the mechanistic understanding remains unclear. Both agree further investigation is needed.

Both support phylogenetic findings about SPARKEL (C175-C176). OpenEval notes C173 about absence of E3 ligase components and that C176's speculation about alternative mechanisms is not directly tested. Peer reviewers accepted the phylogenetic analysis and appropriately framed speculation as hypothesis. Peer review R14 also includes C34-C36 about phylogenetic distribution, which OpenEval addresses in R2.

OpenEval supports background context claims (C1-C2, C121, C128) from prior work, noting these are not primary findings but appropriately cite established literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not separately evaluate background claims.

OpenEval supports established background knowledge (C10-C21) with appropriate citations, noting these contextualize the work but are not primary findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not separately evaluate background literature claims.

OpenEval supports background on mammalian AGC kinase regulation (C122-C127), noting these establish conceptual framework but are not primary findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not separately evaluate background claims about mammalian systems.

OpenEval supports background on AGC kinase functions in apicomplexans (C146-C150, C152-C153) with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not separately evaluate these contextual background claims.

Both support PKA C3-SPARK association (C157). OpenEval addresses this as part of background context (C154-C156) plus primary finding from IP-MS and TurboID. Peer reviewers accepted the association as part of the comprehensive characterization showing SPARK controls PKA C3 function.

OpenEval supports background on Elongin C function (C169-C172) with appropriate citations, noting these contextualize SPARKEL findings but are not primary results. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not separately evaluate these background claims.

OpenEval supports summary/concluding statements (C177-C178, C182), noting C182 is appropriately qualified as speculative but represents reasonable hypothesis. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not separately evaluate these concluding statements, though they endorsed the overall model.

OpenEval supports citations to prior work (C3-C5, C22-C23, C129, C133) that establish rationale for the investigation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not separately evaluate these contextual citations.

OpenEval supports background information and inferences (C28-C30, C37, C84) that contextualize the study. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not separately evaluate these contextual claims.

Both support technical observations (C31, C45). OpenEval notes C31 is supported by sequence analysis and C45 appropriately acknowledges technical limitation of colocalization experiment. Peer reviewers included these claims in their overall endorsement of the SPARK-SPARKEL interaction findings without specific comment on the technical limitations.
